question: According to the FIGO leiomyoma subclassification system, which fibroid type is MOST closely associated with abnormal uterine bleeding due to its distortion of the endometrial cavity?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Type 5 fibroids are predominantly subserosal and rarely cause significant bleeding.
Correct. Submucous fibroids (Types 0–2) distort the endometrial cavity and are the primary cause of menorrhagia in fibroid disease.
Type 6 fibroids are largely subserosal and more commonly cause pressure symptoms than bleeding.
Pedunculated subserosal fibroids do not contact the endometrial cavity and do not typically cause menorrhagia.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: the FIGO system numbers fibroids 0–8 from submucous (cavity-distorting) to subserosal. Bleeding is driven by the submucous types (0–2).
Well done! Submucous fibroids (Types 0–2 in the FIGO system) are the most symptomatic for bleeding because they lie within or immediately adjacent to the endometrial cavity.
